title: Week 4
subtitle: A missed period, and a test with two lines on it. Almost nothing has changed yet, and everything has.

baby.size: About the size of a poppy seed
baby.development: A ball of cells has settled into the lining of your uterus and started making the hormone a test looks for. The neural tube, which becomes the brain and spinal cord, is forming this week.

you.body: You may feel nothing at all, or you may feel like a period is coming. Cramping and light spotting are common in early pregnancy. Your breasts may be tender and your sense of smell may sharpen.
you.mind: Finding out can bring joy, fear, or both in the same minute. All of it is allowed. You do not have to feel a particular way to be doing this right.

coreActions.title: Start a prenatal vitamin with folic acid
coreActions.why: Folic acid lowers the chance of a neural tube defect, and the tube closes in the next few weeks. Starting now is the whole point.
coreActions.detail: Look for 400 micrograms of folic acid on the label. Many prenatal vitamins have more, which is fine. If you have a family history of neural tube defects or take certain seizure medicines, your OB may suggest a higher dose — ask rather than guess. A plain folic acid tablet is enough if a full prenatal upsets your stomach.

options.label: Any prenatal vitamin with 400 mcg folic acid
options.detail: The store brand is the same vitamin. Check the label, not the price.

options.label: A gummy prenatal
options.detail: Easier on the stomach, but most gummies have no iron. Ask about a separate iron source.
options.note: Gummies usually skip iron, which matters more from the second trimester.

options.label: A prescription prenatal
options.detail: Often covered by insurance and usually higher in iron. Ask at your first visit.

questions.question: Does a pill with iron upset your stomach?
questions.why: Iron is the part most likely to cause nausea or constipation.

questions.question: What would you like to spend a month?
Do you have insurance that covers prescriptions?

answers.label: No, or I am not sure

recommendations.reason: A gummy skips the iron that is bothering you. Add a separate iron source once your OB says to.
Covered and higher in iron, which you will need more of later.
The store brand has the same folic acid. The label is what matters.

coreActions.skipIf: You already take a prenatal vitamin, or your OB has prescribed one.

coreActions.title: Take a second test in a few days
coreActions.why: A home test measures a hormone that doubles every couple of days early on. A second line that gets darker is a good sign.
coreActions.detail: Use first-morning urine, when the hormone is most concentrated. You do not need to test every day — two tests a few days apart is enough. If the line gets lighter, or you have bleeding with pain, call your OB rather than testing again.

options.label: Cheap test strips
options.detail: Sold in packs of 20 to 50. Fine for watching a line get darker.

options.label: A digital test
options.detail: Says 'pregnant' in words. No line to read, which some people find calmer.

coreActions.skipIf: Your OB has already confirmed the pregnancy with a blood test.

coreActions.title: Book your first prenatal visit
coreActions.why: Most practices see you between 8 and 10 weeks. Calling now gets you a slot in that window instead of after it.
coreActions.detail: When you call, they will ask the first day of your last period. That date sets your due date until an ultrasound refines it. Ask what to bring: insurance card, a list of medicines, and any family history you know.

options.label: An OB practice
options.detail: A doctor who handles pregnancy and delivery. The most common choice in the US.

options.label: A certified nurse-midwife
options.detail: Often longer visits and a lower rate of intervention. Ask where they deliver.

options.label: A community health center
options.detail: Sliding-scale fees and often a midwife on staff. Good if insurance is uncertain.

coreActions.skipIf: You already have a prenatal appointment booked.

alsoKnow.title: There is no known safe amount of alcohol
alsoKnow.body: The advice is to stop entirely, and the earlier the better. If you drank before you knew, tell your OB. That is a common thing and it is not a reason to panic.

alsoKnow.title: Caffeine has a ceiling, not a ban
alsoKnow.body: Up to about 200 milligrams a day is considered fine — roughly one 12-ounce coffee. Check tea, soda, and chocolate too, because they add up.

alsoKnow.title: Your due date is an estimate, and a rough one
alsoKnow.body: It is 40 weeks from the first day of your last period. Only about 4 in 100 babies arrive on it. An early ultrasound will refine it, and that refined date is the one that sticks.

redFlags.text: Sharp pain on one side, especially with dizziness or shoulder pain
Bleeding that fills a pad, or bleeding with pain

appointments.label: Call to book your first prenatal visit
appointments.note: Most practices book 8 to 10 weeks, so calling now keeps you in the window.
